sentences.zh: 你大学毕业后，友谊就突然消失了。

sentences.en: But something did change clearly as you got older, more into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 但随着你年龄增长，进入成年期，确实有些事情发生了变化。

sentences.en: What were your friendships like in sort of your mid-twenties after you left, after you graduated college?
sentences.zh: 在你大学毕业后的二十五岁左右，你的友谊是什么样的？

sentences.en: Immediately after college, they were amazing, because I was single, living in New York.
sentences.zh: 大学刚毕业时，友谊非常棒，因为我单身，住在纽约。

sentences.en: So, I had various apartments that I shared with different friends.
sentences.zh: 所以我住过不同的公寓，和不同的朋友合租。

sentences.en: And that was like, you know, basically an extension of college, because it was, you know, staying
sentences.zh: 那基本上是大学生活的延续，因为，你知道，每天晚上都熬夜，

sentences.en: up super late every night, often, you know, with beers or weed or whatever, probably both, and tons of takeout that was terrible for us.
sentences.zh: 通常，你知道，喝着啤酒或抽着大麻之类的，可能两者都有，还有一大堆对我们身体很不好的外卖。

sentences.en: And, you know, just, I remember, like, again, having the time of my life in my early twenties
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我记得，再次强调，我在大学毕业后的二十出头时过得非常开心，

sentences.en: after college, like, and it was, like, somewhere around, like, 25, 26, that things began to shift.
sentences.zh: 然后，大约在25、26岁左右，情况开始发生转变。

sentences.en: That was, like, when a lot of my friends and me started to be like, well, we need to get our shit together, right?
sentences.zh: 那时候，我和很多朋友开始觉得，好吧，我们需要振作起来了，对吧？

sentences.en: There was, like, it was, like, this moment.
sentences.zh: 当时有一种，就是那种时刻。

sentences.en: I know exactly, but, yeah, it's the get-your-shit-together years.
sentences.zh: 我非常清楚，是的，这就是所谓的“振作起来”的岁月。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, like, that started happening.
sentences.zh: 所以，事情就是这样开始的。

sentences.en: You know, I had friends who were going to law school, friends who were going to med school.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有朋友要去读法学院，有朋友要去读医学院。

sentences.en: So, this thing started happening where everyone's getting their shit together.
sentences.zh: 所以，每个人都在开始“振作起来”。

sentences.en: People are, like, leaving New York.
sentences.zh: 人们开始离开纽约。

sentences.en: And so, that starts to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以，事情就开始发生了。

sentences.en: And then, the bigger thing, of course, the biggest thing, I would say, is people started, their relationships started to get more and more serious.
sentences.zh: 然后，更重要的事情，当然，我认为最重要的事情是，人们开始，他们的恋爱关系变得越来越认真。

sentences.en: So, I had a girlfriend in college, and we decided to move in together.
sentences.zh: 我在大学时有个女朋友，我们决定同居。

sentences.en: So, now I'm going from, like, living with friends to living with my romantic partner.
sentences.zh: 所以，我现在从和朋友住在一起变成了和我的伴侣住在一起。

sentences.en: And with friends, for the most part, like, you know, you don't really have to, like, check in with them about anything.
sentences.zh: 和朋友在一起时，大部分情况下，你知道，你真的不需要和他们报备任何事情。

sentences.en: You can do whatever the hell you want, right?
sentences.zh: 你可以做任何你想做的事，对吧？

sentences.en: But, um, also, like, with friends, it's, like, none of the dishes are getting done, and we're both slobs, and, like, we don't care.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，同样，和朋友在一起时，碗筷没人洗，我们俩都很邋遢，而且，我们也不在乎。

sentences.en: But, like, when you're in a romantic thing, it's, like, all right, now you've got to take the chores more seriously.
sentences.zh: 但当你处于恋爱关系中时，情况就是，好吧，现在你必须更认真地对待家务了。

sentences.en: You have to, like, you're really sharing a space.
sentences.zh: 你必须，你确实是在共享一个空间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, like, building a home with somebody, and, you know, so you're running your plans by your partner.
sentences.zh: 而且，和某人一起建立一个家，所以你会和你的伴侣商量你的计划。

sentences.en: So, little by little, you move in with your partner, you are going out less, because you already are with your partner, and, like, a big part of going out is, like, oh, well,
sentences.zh: 所以，一点一点地，你和伴侣住在一起，你出门的次数变少了，因为你已经和伴侣在一起了，而且，出门的一个重要原因就是，哦，好吧，

sentences.en: maybe I'll meet the person tonight, you know, at the bar or whatever, and you don't have that anymore.
sentences.zh: 也许我今晚能在酒吧或其他地方遇到那个人，你知道，你不再有那种需求了。

sentences.en: There's less of a drive, yeah.
sentences.zh: 动力确实减少了，是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, when you're with, like, you know, the love of your life, and you can see them whenever you want, this idea starts to creep in, well, like, what do I even need
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当你和你的挚爱在一起，而且你可以随时见到他们时，这个念头就开始悄悄出现，好吧，我还需要

sentences.en: my friends for?
sentences.zh: 我的朋友做什么呢？

sentences.en: Like, I got everything right here, right?
sentences.zh: 就像，我这里已经拥有一切了，对吧？

sentences.en: I have, like, somebody who I love to talk to.
sentences.zh: 我有，比如，一个我喜欢聊天的人。

sentences.en: I also get to do other stuff with them.
sentences.zh: 我还可以和他们一起做其他事情。

sentences.en: Exactly, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，对吧。

sentences.en: And it's all in the same package, and, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且这一切都在同一个包里，你知道的。

sentences.en: It's, like, when this was happening, this moving in with your partner who becomes, or your girlfriend, rather, who becomes your wife, and this sort of slowly, I don't want to

sentences.en: say, like, the friendships becoming less and less central to your life, maybe less and less of a priority.
sentences.zh: 说，友谊在你的生活中变得越来越不重要，也许越来越不是优先事项。

sentences.en: Were you aware of that?
sentences.zh: 你意识到这一点了吗？

sentences.en: I was definitely aware of it, because some of my friends were giving me grief about it.
sentences.zh: 我绝对意识到了，因为我的一些朋友为此抱怨我。

sentences.en: Oh, look at Sam.
sentences.zh: 哦，看看Sam。

sentences.en: Like, you know, now that he's got, you know, he lives with his girlfriend, like, he doesn't have time for us anymore.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，现在他有了，你知道，他和女朋友住在一起，他再也没有时间陪我们了。

sentences.en: You know, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是那种事。

sentences.en: I was, I mean, the honest truth is that at the time, I didn't consciously miss my friends that much.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，诚实地说，当时我并没有自觉地那么想念我的朋友。

sentences.en: I was so excited about being with my romantic partner and, like, so focused on, like, trying to crush shit and getting my shit together, all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我当时太兴奋能和我的伴侣在一起了，而且太专注于，比如，努力工作和振作起来，所有那些事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I wasn't really, if anything, like, I was annoyed at my friends for guilt tripping me.
sentences.zh: 我并没有，如果有的话，我反而因为朋友们让我感到内疚而感到恼火。

sentences.en: I'm like, ah, just get over it, dude.
sentences.zh: 我就想，啊，算了吧，伙计。

sentences.en: And, i.e., like, get your own girlfriend and, like, leave me alone, right?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，去找你自己的女朋友，然后别烦我，对吧？

sentences.en: I didn't literally say that, but I was thinking something along those lines.
sentences.zh: 我没有真的那样说，但我当时确实是这么想的。

sentences.en: Becoming mature involved getting a romantic partner and, like, not goofing around with your friends.
sentences.zh: 变得成熟意味着要有一个伴侣，而不是和朋友瞎混。

sentences.en: Like, you're not really a man unless you, like, stop hanging out with your friends.
sentences.zh: 就像，除非你不再和朋友鬼混，否则你就不算是个真正的男人。

sentences.en: Or, like, hone in, yeah, or hone in on this person who you love.
sentences.zh: 或者，比如，专注于，是的，专注于你所爱的那个人。

sentences.en: I mean, it's making me think about how, you know, we sort of talk about this on the show,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这让我想起，你知道，我们在节目中谈论过这个，

sentences.en: but it's like you were getting all these different things from different people earlier on in your life.
sentences.zh: 但就像你在生命早期从不同的人那里得到了所有这些不同的东西。

sentences.en: You're getting fun from your friends and emotional support from, you know, this guy and basketball with this other guy.
sentences.zh: 你从朋友那里得到乐趣，从这个家伙那里得到情感支持，和另一个人一起打篮球。

sentences.en: And then it's like, it's just sort of your focus narrows and you meet this romantic partner who you love, you love deeply, and sort of the emotional and the physical and the fun

sentences.zh: 就像你把太多的东西寄托在恋爱关系上，以至于友谊看起来像是一种干扰，我听到的几乎就是这个意思。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 就像，好吧，如果我连续两周不出门，吃得健康，不熬夜喝酒，做一个好伴侣，那么，我就放纵一下。

sentences.zh: 这几乎就像吃垃圾食品一样，对吧？

sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.zh: 那Rob在这期间在哪里？

sentences.zh: 当你和伴侣同居时，他怎么样了？

sentences.zh: 你们还有联系吗？

sentences.zh: 所以，Rob在大学毕业后也搬到了纽约市。

sentences.zh: 在某个时候，他搬回了波士顿。

sentences.en: And we were still communicating on the phone and writing each other these, like, long emails.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然通过电话交流，并给彼此写那些，比如，很长的电子邮件。

sentences.en: Like, we would write each other, like, three or four or 5,000 word emails.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们会给彼此写三四千甚至五千字的邮件。

sentences.en: Wow, whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇，天哪。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 其中一些邮件在情感上非常成熟。

sentences.zh: 你们在聊什么？

sentences.zh: 以一种令人惊讶的方式。

sentences.zh: 你知道，你做的这件事真的伤害了我。

sentences.zh: 这是我的感受。

sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这些事情比我现在与男性朋友互动的方式要成熟得多。

sentences.en: But we were still doing that into our mid-20s.
sentences.zh: 但我们在二十多岁时还在这样做。

sentences.en: But, yeah, so Rob was in Boston.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，所以Rob当时在波士顿。

sentences.zh: 而且，是的，在那时候，我很多最好的朋友都已经各奔东西了。

sentences.en: And then life continues to happen.

sentences.zh: 然后结婚了。

sentences.zh: 恭喜。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Marriage is just like the relationship thing, but on steroids because you're like, well, now I'm married.
sentences.zh: 婚姻就像恋爱关系一样，但强度加倍，因为你会觉得，好吧，现在我结婚了。

sentences.en: So, like, I mean, of course there were no, like, actual rules saying, well, you can't go see your friends now that you're married.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，当然没有什么硬性规定说，你结婚了就不能去见朋友了。

sentences.en: But there's this internalized idea.
sentences.zh: 但内心深处有一种潜移默化的观念。

sentences.en: It's like, well, you know, now that you're a husband, you should be spending a lot more time at home and not out with your friends.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你知道，既然你已经是个丈夫了，你就应该花更多时间待在家里，而不是出去和朋友鬼混。

sentences.en: Where did you learn that from?
sentences.zh: 你是从哪儿学到这些的？

sentences.en: Like, where were you, who or what, or where were you getting that message from?
sentences.zh: 比如，你当时在哪儿，是谁或者什么东西，或者你是从哪儿接收到这些信息的？

sentences.en: I'm just curious.
sentences.zh: 我只是好奇。

sentences.en: I think, I think the best way I can answer that is that it was, it was just vibes.
sentences.zh: 我想，我想我能给出的最好回答是，这只是一种氛围。

sentences.en: It was like vibes that come down from years and years and years of watching movies and TV shows and all kinds of messages about, like,
sentences.zh: 这就像是多年来通过看电影、电视节目以及各种信息所潜移默化形成的氛围，关于，比如，

sentences.en: this is what a boy does and this is what a man does.
sentences.zh: 男孩该做什么，男人又该做什么。

sentences.en: And a grown man who continues to, like, hang out with his friends is a man child, right?
sentences.zh: 而一个成年男人如果还继续和朋友混在一起，那就是个“巨婴”，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A grown man is supposed to be at home with his wife or out there crushing and making a lot of money so he can be the breadwinner and bring home a lot.
sentences.zh: 一个成年男人应该待在家里陪妻子，或者在外面拼搏赚钱，好成为家里的顶梁柱，带回丰厚的收入。

sentences.en: You know, that's the kind of message over and over and over you're getting from these various, like, cultural inputs, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是你从各种文化输入中一遍又一遍接收到的信息，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, this is the way it's supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 就像是，事情本该如此。

sentences.en: And then having kids, all of a sudden now you actually are insanely busy.
sentences.zh: 然后有了孩子，突然之间，你变得忙得不可开交。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I say right like I know, but I haven't had any kids yet.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我虽然附和着说“没错”，好像我很懂一样，但我还没生过孩子。

sentences.en: You get it.
sentences.zh: 你懂的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You're insanely busy.
sentences.zh: 你忙得不可开交。

sentences.en: For the first time in your life, you actually truly cannot do whatever the hell you want.
sentences.zh: 这是你人生中第一次，你真的无法随心所欲地做任何事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You kind of can't do whatever you want when you're married because it's rude to your partner.
sentences.zh: 结婚后你其实也不能随心所欲，因为那样对伴侣很不尊重。

sentences.en: But, like, if you do whatever you want when you have a kid, like, the kid will starve and die.
sentences.zh: 但如果你有了孩子还随心所欲，那孩子可能会饿死。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like, you can't, you know, the thing I was not prepared for among many things was, like, just the amount of dishes and laundry that I was doing.
sentences.zh: 比如，你无法……你知道，我没准备好的事情有很多，其中之一就是我做的那些洗碗和洗衣服的家务量。

sentences.en: Just, like, endless amounts of cleaning up.
sentences.zh: 就是没完没了的清理工作。

sentences.en: And then you're not sleeping for years.
sentences.zh: 而且你还得好几年睡不好觉。

sentences.en: Sorry to scare you off from having kids.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，吓到你不敢生孩子了。

sentences.en: No, it's good.
sentences.zh: 不，没关系。

sentences.en: That's good to hear.
sentences.zh: 听到你这么说真好。

sentences.en: You quickly – well, I say you get used to it.
sentences.zh: 你很快——好吧，我说你很快就会习惯。

sentences.en: You don't get used to it.
sentences.zh: 其实你根本习惯不了。

sentences.en: So you really do have less time to hang out with your friends at that point.
sentences.zh: 所以到那个阶段，你确实没时间去和朋友聚会了。

sentences.en: But what ended up happening was I was saying no to friends more or just, like,
sentences.zh: 但最后发生的情况是，我更多地拒绝了朋友，或者只是，

sentences.en: not reaching out to friends as much because I was genuinely swamped and I was tired and I didn't want to go out at night.
sentences.zh: 没那么常联系朋友了，因为我真的忙得焦头烂额，而且我很累，晚上不想出门。

sentences.en: It makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这说得通。

sentences.en: I wanted to try to get a good night's sleep or whatever, right?
sentences.zh: 我想试着睡个好觉之类的，对吧？

sentences.en: But the part where it started to get truly, like, corrosive to my friendships was, okay, things start getting a little bit easier with the kids.
sentences.zh: 但真正开始对我的友谊产生腐蚀作用的部分是，好吧，孩子的情况开始好转了。

sentences.en: Like, they get sleep trained.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们养成了睡眠习惯。

sentences.en: Now I'm sleeping better.
sentences.zh: 现在我睡得好多了。

sentences.en: I'm in more of a routine where I know how to do the laundry faster and, like, I do have a little bit more free time on my hands.
sentences.zh: 我的生活更有规律了，我知道怎么更快地洗衣服，而且我确实多出了一点空闲时间。

sentences.en: But, uh-oh, it's been months since I hung out with a friend.
sentences.zh: 但是，糟糕，我已经好几个月没和朋友聚过了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Do I even know how to hang out with a friend anymore?
sentences.zh: 我甚至还知道怎么和朋友相处吗？

sentences.en: Like, what are we even going to talk about?
sentences.zh: 比如，我们还能聊些什么呢？

sentences.en: Okay, that's what I want to focus on.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是我想关注的重点。

sentences.en: It's like, was there a moment where you kind of looked up – I mean, it's the blur of children and obligations, all these legitimate things, of course –
sentences.zh: 就像是，有没有那么一刻，你抬头看看——我是说，在孩子和各种义务的忙乱中，当然，这些都是正当的事情——

sentences.en: and said, like, oh my god, it's been months since I've seen Rob or insert other friend here.
sentences.zh: 然后说，天哪，我已经好几个月没见过 Rob 或者其他朋友了。

sentences.en: Like, how did that realization come to you?
sentences.zh: 这种觉悟是怎么产生的？

sentences.en: And what did it feel like?
sentences.zh: 当时是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Well, I started joking around with my wife, you know, look at me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我开始和妻子开玩笑，你知道，看看我。

sentences.en: I'm, like, becoming one of these cliche data points of, like, the lonely American male.
sentences.zh: 我快要成为那种孤独的美国男性的陈词滥调数据点了。

sentences.en: But it was still kind of a joke that I didn't quite take seriously.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然像是个玩笑，我并没有太当真。

sentences.en: And then, at a certain point, I just started feeling like, um, oh, wait a second, this is actually a problem.
sentences.zh: 然后，在某个时刻，我开始觉得，嗯，等等，这其实是个问题。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Like many, many new parents, I was arguing, you know, with my wife about our kids, you know, and, like, who did the – you know,
sentences.zh: 像许多许多新手父母一样，我当时在和妻子争论关于孩子的事，你知道，还有，谁做了——你知道，

sentences.en: who did less of this responsibility and who is owed more of this?
sentences.zh: 谁承担的责任更少，谁又该承担更多？

sentences.en: And it was – it was exactly the kind of emotional moment in my life that I really should have reached out to other friends who were going through the exact same thing that I was going through.
sentences.zh: 那正是那种我本该向其他正经历同样困境的朋友寻求帮助的情感时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because I had other friends who had kids pretty much at the exact same time as I did.
sentences.zh: 因为我确实有其他朋友，他们几乎和我同时有了孩子。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And I wasn't reaching out to them.
sentences.zh: 但我没有联系他们。

sentences.en: I just – I wasn't – I had no one to – especially if, like, my wife and I were in a place where, you know, we had just gotten into an argument or something.
sentences.zh: 我只是——我没法——我没人可以——特别是如果我和妻子正处于那种，你知道，刚吵完架之类的状态。

sentences.en: Like, what am I going to do?
sentences.zh: 我能怎么办？

sentences.en: Just, like, talk to my wife about how hard it was that I got into an argument?
sentences.zh: 难道要跟妻子抱怨我吵架有多难受吗？

sentences.en: Well, I was going to say, let's take that sort of example.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我正想说，我们拿这个例子来说。

sentences.en: Would you, like, go to your phone and think about texting or calling a friend and then just be like, I mean – like, take me through that thought process.
sentences.zh: 你会拿起手机，想给朋友发短信或打电话，然后又觉得——我是说，带我走一遍那个心理过程。

sentences.en: What would you do?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么做？

sentences.en: I mean – it's funny.
sentences.zh: 我是说——这很有趣。

sentences.en: I would, like, go to my phone, be like, I – I'm going to text my friend and see, you know, if he's around to talk.
sentences.zh: 我会拿起手机，心想，我要给朋友发个短信，看看他有没有空聊聊。

sentences.en: And then, like, I would be like, ah, do I really want to get into it?
sentences.zh: 然后，我会想，啊，我真的想聊这个吗？

sentences.en: And then I'd be like, ah, like, do I really want to, like, impose my whining on my friend who's also got his own shit going on?
sentences.zh: 然后我会想，啊，我真的想把我的抱怨强加给那个也有自己烦心事的朋友吗？

sentences.en: And, like, you know – you know what?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道——你知道吗？

sentences.en: Oh, look, there's a new episode of this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 哦，看，这个播客出了新的一集。

sentences.en: Click.
sentences.zh: 点击。

sentences.en: And then I end up listening to a podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 然后我就去听播客了。

sentences.en: And I just ended up listening to a tremendous number of podcasts instead of calling friends.
sentences.zh: 结果我听了大量的播客，而不是给朋友打电话。

sentences.en: That is – that is – like, it feels like the most cliched thing ever, but that is actually what happened to me.
sentences.zh: 这真是——这真是——听起来简直是陈词滥调，但这确实就是发生在我身上的事。

sentences.en: Tell me what shows you were turning to.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你都在听什么节目。

sentences.en: What were you listening to instead of calling a friend?
sentences.zh: 你当时在听什么，而不是给朋友打电话？

sentences.en: So, I started out actually listening to, like, podcasts about meditation because I had heard that meditation was good for you and, like –
sentences.zh: 所以，我一开始其实是在听关于冥想的播客，因为我听说冥想对你有好处，而且——

sentences.en: When you have small kids, certainly, of course.
sentences.zh: 当你有了小孩，当然，确实如此。

sentences.en: And then, like, you know, started going – I wouldn't call it a rabbit hole, but, you know, I started, like –
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，开始——我不会称之为陷入泥潭，但你知道，我开始——

sentences.en: eventually, like, I started listening to the Joe Rogan experience because he just has had everyone on his show.
sentences.zh: 最终，我开始听《乔·罗根体验》(Joe Rogan Experience)，因为他节目里什么人都请过。

sentences.en: And he's talking for, like, four and a half hours.
sentences.zh: 而且他一聊就是四个半小时。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: He's talking for a long, long, long time.
sentences.zh: 他聊了很长很长的时间。

sentences.en: But, you know, like, he'd have astrophysicists on his show.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，他会请天体物理学家上节目。

sentences.en: He'd have Michael Pollan, whose book I had just read and really wanted to hear more from Michael Pollan on his show.
sentences.zh: 他请过迈克尔·波伦 (Michael Pollan)，我刚读过他的书，真的很想在节目里多听听他的见解。

sentences.en: He had this Stanford professor talking about dopamine and addiction science.
sentences.zh: 他还请过一位斯坦福大学教授谈论多巴胺和成瘾科学。

sentences.en: And, you know, so I would listen to his shows just to, you know, try to pick up, you know, whatever, life hacks or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以，我听他的节目只是为了，你知道，试着学点什么生活小窍门之类的。

sentences.en: And, you know, again, the reason I'm doing this is because, like, I'm feeling overwhelmed, lonely, all of these feelings.
sentences.zh: 而且，再说一次，我这么做是因为我感到不知所措、孤独，所有这些情绪。

sentences.en: And instead of relating to, you know, other people and calling a friend, I'm like, well, I can just solve these problems on my own.
sentences.zh: 与其与人交流、给朋友打电话，我心想，好吧，我可以自己解决这些问题。

sentences.en: I'll just listen to some podcasts and I'll get the answers from the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我听听播客，就能从播客里得到答案。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I can do this all on my own.
sentences.zh: 我可以独自搞定这一切。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's this kind of rogue self-sufficiency, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一种孤狼式的自给自足，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I'm not feeling so good emotionally or whatever.
sentences.zh: 就像，我情绪不太好之类的。

sentences.en: And I want to address this.
sentences.zh: 我想解决这个问题。

sentences.en: But, you know, I'm going to fix this myself by listening and learning and working on myself.
sentences.zh: 但是，我要通过倾听、学习和自我提升来自己解决它。

sentences.en: There was something in the Rogan thing that appealed to me, which was basically, like, stop making excuses, man up, you know, I'm using that in air quotes, but, like, man up.
sentences.zh: 罗根节目里有些东西吸引了我，基本上就是，别找借口，像个男人一样——我这是加了引号的——但就是“像个男人一样”。

sentences.en: And, basically, the easiest thing you could do right now to change your life, all of these podcasts said this, go work out.
sentences.zh: 基本上，所有这些播客都说，你现在能做的改变生活的最简单的事，就是去健身。

sentences.en: Go work out.
sentences.zh: 去健身。

sentences.en: Stop.
sentences.zh: 停下来。

sentences.en: Get out of your head.
sentences.zh: 别再胡思乱想了。

sentences.en: Pump some goddamn iron.
sentences.zh: 去举举铁吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, and they all said this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们都这么说。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 我就想，哦，那很有趣。

sentences.en: Like, maybe I should try that.
sentences.zh: 也许我应该试试。

sentences.en: You know, like, if you just take care of your body, not only are you going to get healthier, but, like, everything else in your life is going to fall into place.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你照顾好自己的身体，不仅会变得更健康，而且生活中的其他一切也会步入正轨。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think, in a way, part of the reason why it appealed so much is, like, I knew that even though it's really hard to, like, exercise all the time and, you know, lift heavy weights,
sentences.zh: 我觉得在某种程度上，它之所以如此吸引我，是因为我知道，尽管一直锻炼、举重真的很辛苦，

sentences.en: I knew that on some level it was easier than doing deep emotional work.
sentences.zh: 但我知道在某种层面上，这比进行深度的情感交流要容易得多。

sentences.en: So I was like, well, all right, I'll just try that.
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，好吧，我就试试这个。

sentences.en: And it was like, what was I doing in my late 30s and early 40s every spare moment I had?
sentences.zh: 那我在三十多岁到四十出头的时候，每一刻空闲时间都在做什么？

sentences.en: I was exercising.
sentences.zh: 我在锻炼。

sentences.en: I was going to CrossFit.
sentences.zh: 我在做 CrossFit 训练。

sentences.en: I was running outside in Prospect Park through freezing cold rain.
sentences.zh: 我在展望公园 (Prospect Park) 的冰冷雨中跑步。

sentences.en: Because, you know, I had this idea that, like, well, at least if I'm doing this, I'll, you know, I'll be able to, like, basically conquer whatever lonely feelings I'm having.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，我有个想法，至少如果我这么做，我就能基本上克服我所感受到的任何孤独感。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: Physical sublimation.
sentences.zh: 身体上的升华。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it was the idea, basically, that, like, life was to be crushed, not to be enjoyed.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是一种观念：生活是用来征服的，而不是用来享受的。

sentences.en: I mean, and it also is a, it's a solitary, it's like, go and lift this thing, and then when that gets easy, lift it heavier.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这也是一种孤独的活动，就像是，去举起这个东西，当它变轻了，就举更重的。

sentences.en: The power is within you to change you.
sentences.zh: 改变自己的力量就在你心中。

sentences.en: And it's still very, like, individual-focused, intrapersonal.
sentences.zh: 而且它仍然非常注重个人，是内省的。

sentences.en: So I can see why it would appeal.
sentences.zh: 所以我能明白为什么它会有吸引力。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess I wonder, like, was this a conscious choice on your end to turn, like, towards these podcasts or working out or whatever instead of friends?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我很好奇，你转向这些播客或健身之类的，而不是找朋友，这是一种有意识的选择吗？

sentences.en: Like, were you aware that you were diverting sort of in that way?
sentences.zh: 你是否意识到自己在以那种方式转移注意力？

sentences.en: I don't think I was aware of it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我没意识到。

sentences.en: I think, I think I was still telling myself, you know, you don't have time for friends because you're so busy.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我当时还在告诉自己，你没时间陪朋友，因为你太忙了。

sentences.en: I was also in denial about being lonely, right?
sentences.zh: 我也在否认自己感到孤独的事实，对吧？

sentences.en: I just knew that I felt, I felt bad and I wanted to feel good.
sentences.zh: 我只知道我感觉不好，我想感觉好一点。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, well, if I exercise, I'll feel good.
sentences.zh: 我就想，哦，如果我锻炼，我就会感觉好些。

sentences.en: And I did feel good temporarily.
sentences.zh: 我确实暂时感觉好了一些。

sentences.en: There were the endorphins that they promised me would happen.
sentences.zh: 有他们承诺过会产生的内啡肽。

sentences.en: And then they came.
sentences.zh: 然后它们确实来了。

sentences.en: I think that's a really important point.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常重要的观点。

sentences.en: And I really think that there is still something very icky and, like,
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得这依然是一件非常令人不适的事情，而且，就像是，

sentences.en: we're allergic to self-identifying as lonely because it's very vulnerable to admit that not only to yourself but also out loud.
sentences.zh: 我们对承认自己感到孤独有一种过敏反应，因为承认这一点不仅是对自己，甚至是大声说出来，都是非常脆弱的表现。

sentences.en: So, first of all, thanks for saying that.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先，谢谢你这么说。

sentences.en: But I understand why it would be shielded in these layers of I'm not the kind of person that gets lonely.
sentences.zh: 但我明白为什么它会被层层包裹，伪装成“我不是那种会感到孤独的人”。

sentences.en: And also, like, look, there's this whole thing in the culture of the incel, right?
